world_status: statement found in an open source
sweep_summary: Nobiin is not in the catalog. The sole title-keyword item, Barzilai 2019 (workshop talk, Glottolog 596418, no URL), could not be obtained; the author's own 2021 ACAL paper (held by the project) shows it concerns liquid epenthesis at prosodic-constituent boundaries, not word stress — relevance prosody-but-not-word-stress, priority low. New this search of works with stress in the title: Dingemanse 2005 'A sketch of Nobiin tone' retrieved from an Internet Archive copy of the author's site; its sec. 2.3 reports Werner 1987: 77 that no accent phenomena were perceived and that Nobiin is a two-tone (H/L) language with moraic TBU — consistent with the Werner p. 64 snippet and the SPA/Bell 1971 'tonal accent, location unpredictable' entry already held by the project. The only first-hand positive 'accent' rules remain Reinisch 1879 paras 71-73 (pre-tonal, three-syllable window, weight-sensitive). Werner 1987 pp. 64-77 is the priority acquisition if a first-hand stress statement is wanted.

new_statements.translation: 2 Tonal distinctions. Nobiin has two tone levels, High (H) and Low (T). A combination of these tonemes yields the falling tone (F = HT), but not a rising tone, which Bell assumed for one lexeme (1970: 28). ... accent is not drawn on to explain tonal changes or phenomena. Whether and in what way stress (Druckakzent) plays a role in Nobiin remains outside this investigation. [p.64] ... Tonemes: H, L and F. ... All three tonemes (including F) can occur on short and long, open and closed syllables [p.65].

new_statements.rule_in_words: Nobiin is described as a two-level tone language (H vs L, plus a falling HL contour on a single syllable); tone is lexically contrastive and any syllable type may carry any tone; the grammar of record explicitly declines to say whether a stress accent exists, and no modern source states a stress position. The same two-tone, no-stress-claim picture is stated first-hand in two open sources saved here (Barzilai & Khalil 2021 p.3 'Nobiin contrasts between H and L tones'; Oakley 2021 p.263 'Nobiin has two contrastive level tones: H and ∅.. realized as L'). SPA 1979 (after Bell 1971) reads the data as a 'tonal accent system' with the location of the single H in polysyllables lexically unpredictable. The only positional 'accent' rules in print are pre-tonal: Reinisch 1879 §§71-74 (pp.15-16) — accent within the last three syllables, disyllables penult unless the final vowel is long, trisyllables antepenult unless a long vowel or geminate-closed penult draws it — which Werner (p.50) reinterprets as high tone.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None mentioned in any source seen.
new_statements.exceptions: Werner p.64: no rising tone (contra Bell's one lexeme). Reinisch 1879 (pre-tonal): accent shifts to the stem-final syllable before the object particle -ga/-ka and consonant-initial monosyllabic postpositions (§75-76); in Fadidscha-Mahas enclitic particles/postpositions are accented like independent words (§79, §82); plural suffixes attract the accent from final-accented and monosyllabic nouns (§80); compounds keep each member's accent (§83).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level lexical tone in citation forms; Hāshim (Arabic orthography book, pp.51-52) and Werner's review of earlier authors (p.56 snippet) note that pitch realization depends strongly on the word's position in the sentence. Werner's statement is from snippet view only (three overlapping snippets of pp.64-65); the ellipses mark snippet boundaries, not omissions within a sentence.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe Nobiin proper (glottocode nobi1240; also called Mahas, Fadicca/Fadidja/Fiyadikka, Halfawi). Reinisch 1879 treats Kenzi-Dongolawi and Fadidscha-Mahas in one grammar, flagging FM-specific accent behaviour (§§79, 82); his general accent rules are not dialect-tagged. Barzilai & Khalil 2021 and Oakley 2021 are based on diaspora speakers recorded in Washington DC (co-author Nubantood Khalil is a Sudanese Nobiin speaker). Werner 1987 is based on Sudanese Nobiin (Mahas).

new_statements.quote: Finally, with regard to stress in Nobiin, Werner (W:77) remarks that he did not perceive any accent phenomena and that he does not see any reason to tie the account of tone to anything of the sort, concluding that "[d]em Ton muss im Nobiin also ein hoher funktionaler Stellenwert zugemessen werden". [...] Nobiin has two underlying tones, H and L. The falling contour tone occurs only in well-defined contexts (most often in pre-pausal position) [...] the tone bearing unit in Nobiin is the mora. (sec. 2.2, p. 5)
new_statements.translation: German clause: 'Tone must therefore be assigned a high functional value in Nobiin.'
new_statements.citation: Dingemanse, Mark. 2005. A sketch of Nobiin tone. Unpublished report (data from Werner 1987, Grammatik des Nobiin), 16 pp. — sec. 2.3 'Stress, accent and the history of tone in Nobiin', reporting Werner 1987: 77
new_statements.reading: Nobiin is a two-tone (H/L) language with the mora as TBU; Werner 1987 (the only modern full grammar, single-informant fieldwork) perceived no stress/accent phenomena at all and explicitly left stress outside his account (cf. the Google Books snippet already held by the project, Werner 1987: 64 'Ob und in welcher Weise Druckakzent im Nobiin eine Rolle spielt, bleibt ausserhalb dieser Untersuchung'). So there is no positive word-stress rule for Nobiin in the modern literature; the only first-hand 'accent' rules are Reinisch 1879, Grammatik paras 71-73 (held by the project, pp. 15-16: accent on one of the last three syllables; disyllables penultimate unless the final vowel is long; trisyllables antepenultimate when the last two syllables are short, otherwise on the long-vowel or pre-geminate syllable), which Werner later reinterprets as H-tone placement. Caveat: the Dingemanse passage is a second-hand report of Werner's first-hand finding; Werner's own p. 77 was not opened.

sources.quote: There are other documented phonological processes in Nobiin that have been analyzed as preserving input prosodic structure in the output. In a phonological process independent from the assimilation analyzed here, liquids are epenthesized before vowel-initial words, even when the preceding word ends in a consonant and therefore epenthesis results in a consonant cluster. This ... has been analyzed as prosodic faithfulness: epenthetic liquids ensure that syllable boundaries coincide with the prosodic boundaries between morphosyntactic constituents (Barzilai 2019). [Barzilai & Khalil 2021: 8, fn. 6]
sources.locator: Glottolog record 596418 (no URL/DOI); content characterized in Barzilai & Khalil 2021, sec. 2.2 p.3 and fn. 6 p.8 (held by the project:)
sources.note: Unpublished workshop talk; no copy or abstract located (Glottolog record has no URL; The citing paper by the same author (Barzilai & Khalil 2021, read held by the project) describes the talk as an analysis of liquid epenthesis at prosodic-phrase / morphosyntactic-constituent boundaries ('prosodic faithfulness' = syllable-boundary alignment), i.e. segmental process x prosodic structure, not word-stress placement. The 2021 paper itself states only 'Nobiin contrasts between H and L tones' (p.3) and never mentions stress.
